title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is solving a system (33)-(35) in unknowns xi, eta (sections of SL_2 = SG(M) over a base S, M of rank 2) and a scalar mu, which he calls the 'multiplicateur'. The eta-equations are linked to xi by eta = xi.eps_1(1-mu), where eps_1(lambda) is a one-parameter unipotent family. The constraints are det = 1 and trace conditions Tr(xi rho) = Tr rho and Tr(eta sigma) = Tr sigma. In the case actually treated (next page), rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6 and sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has order 4. These are the standard torsion generators of SL_2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. So this is a 2-dimensional, SL_2-valued model of the 'loop equations' (the GT-type braid/pentagon-hexagon relations), with mu playing the role of the cyclotomic exponent.

This page does three things.

(1) Symmetry of the two resolutions. The previous page solved in xi: det xi = 1, Tr xi rho = Tr rho, P(xi) invertible, mu = c/P(xi). The NB there notes that solving in eta gives a parallel system. Here he checks that c' = lambda'_0 c (with lambda'_0 = 1/lambda_0), so c is invertible iff c' is. The eta-system is then det eta = 1, Tr eta sigma = Tr sigma, P'(eta) invertible, mu = c'/P'(eta). The hypotheses are thus symmetric in xi and eta, and the solution scheme can be parametrized either way.

(2) Explicit computation of P(xi). Write eps_1(lambda) = 1 + lambda N_1 = (1+N_1)^lambda. This identity requires N_1 to be nilpotent, N_1^2 = 0. Then, by linearity of the trace,
Tr(xi eps_1(1-mu) sigma) - Tr sigma = Tr xi sigma - Tr sigma + (1-mu) Tr(xi N_1 sigma).
The initial condition (40 bis) reads (1+N_1) sigma = -lambda_0 rho, i.e. (49) N_1 = -(lambda_0 rho sigma^{-1} + 1), or N_1 sigma = -(lambda_0 rho + sigma). Then Tr xi(N_1 sigma + sigma) = -lambda_0 Tr xi rho = -lambda_0 Tr rho, a constant. Solving the eta trace condition for mu gives mu.P(xi) = c with:
- (47)/(50): P(xi) = -Tr(xi N_1 sigma) = Tr xi(lambda_0 rho + sigma);
- c = lambda_0 Tr rho + Tr sigma.

(3) Concrete check. With lambda_0 = 1 we get rho sigma^{-1} = -[[1,0],[1,1]], so N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]] and eps_1(lambda) = [[1,0],[lambda,1]]. Also lambda_0 rho + sigma = [[0,0],[0,1]], so P(xi) = D, as found on the next page, and eta = xi.[[1,0],[1-mu,1]]. The next page concludes that the solution scheme is relatively smooth of relative dimension 2. It is the open subset 'P(xi) invertible' of the smooth curve-fibration {det = 1, Tr xi rho = const} inside SL_2.
errors: The page as transcribed says 'N_1 une matrice de carré unité, N_1^2 = 1'. This is incompatible with eps_1(lambda) = 1 + N_1 lambda = (1+N_1)^lambda: if N_1^2 = 1, then (1+N_1)^2 = 2(1+N_1). The intended (and verified) condition is N_1^2 = 0; with rho, sigma as on the next page, N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]]. Either Grothendieck wrote 'carré nul' and the transcription misreads it, or it is a slip.

The underbrace label under (-N_1 sigma) is transcribed 'N_1 rho^# = rho + sigma'. Mathematically it should read -N_1 sigma = lambda_0 rho + sigma, matching (50) on the next page. As transcribed it is wrong or misread.
Minor: the identity (1+N_1)^lambda = 1 + lambda N_1 for non-integer lambda (e.g. lambda in Z-hat or in O_S) needs N_1 nilpotent so that the binomial series truncates. This is implicit.

ideas.what: Symmetric (xi- or eta-) parametrization of the solution scheme of the SL_2 'loop equation' system, with invertible constants c, c' = lambda'_0 c
ideas.modern_name: explicit SL_2-representation-variety model of GT-type relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (GT-in-SL_2 / representation-variety approaches; Ihara, Drinfeld setting)

ideas.what: Computing the multiplier via a linear trace form: mu.P(xi) = c with P(xi) = Tr xi(lambda_0 rho + sigma), using a unipotent one-parameter group eps_1(lambda) = (1+N_1)^lambda
ideas.modern_name: elementary linear algebra / trace identities in SL_2

ideas.what: Use of the order-4 and order-6 generators sigma, rho of SL_2(Z) with rho sigma^{-1} = minus a unipotent
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche discuss SL_2(Z) and the Teichmüller tower; this specific computation unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the scheme of solutions of a 2-dimensional (SL_2) version of the loop equations, with the cyclotomic-type multiplier mu as a regular function on it. He proves (next page) that this scheme is relatively smooth of dimension 2. The page itself is routine computation inside that larger, apparently unpublished program of studying 'variations on the loop equation' via explicit linear models.
missed.quote: les hypothèses faites sont en fait symétriques en ξ, η, et permettent un traitement symétrique de la résolution
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete SL_2-shadow of GT relations. It could be compared with modern work on GT acting on representation/character varieties, but nothing on this page alone is new.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear-algebra step (computing P(xi) and noting the xi/eta symmetry) inside an unpublished SL_2 model of the loop equations. The broader program is of historical interest, but this page has no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'N_1 une matrice de carré unité, N_1^2 = 1' should almost certainly read 'de carré nul, N_1^2 = 0' (required by eps_1(lambda) = (1+N_1)^lambda and verified by N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]]).
Underbrace annotation 'N_1 rho^# = rho + sigma' is likely '= lambda_0 rho + sigma'.
'sont un fait symétriques' should be 'sont en fait symétriques'; 'une traitement' should be 'un traitement'.
In (47) the sign before Tr is '-' (an overwritten '=' sign).
